summary: Created six frontend planning labels and five unassigned GitHub issues in the agreed delivery order.

artifacts.description: area: frontend; type: discovery; type: design; type: coordination; phase: experience; priority: high
Issues #1 through #5 for plan review, page architecture, visual language, work allocation, and peer review.

acceptance.criterion: The label set distinguishes frontend scope, planning/discovery/design/coordination work, experience phase, and priority without duplicating existing labels.
acceptance.evidence: GitHub label listing shows six newly created labels alongside the pre-existing defaults.

acceptance.criterion: Issues express the agreed dependency order: plan review, page architecture, visual language, work allocation, then page design and peer revision.
acceptance.evidence: Issues #1–#5 were created in that order with dependencies described in their bodies.

acceptance.criterion: Issues are unassigned, linked to the available design documentation, and do not claim unapproved implementation or data behavior.
acceptance.evidence: GitHub issue listing shows empty assignees; issue bodies reference the accepted documentation and defer unapproved contracts/decisions.

checks.name: GitHub label and issue verification
checks.evidence: gh label list and gh issue list confirmed all six labels and five open issues with the expected labels and no assignees.

risks: Individual page implementation issues and assignees must be created after the frontend team completes the ownership plan in issue #4.
followUps: Assign issue #1 to the frontend lead/reviewer; assign the later issues after their dependencies are accepted.
